title: Build Numbers from Factors

voice.baseline_approval: Owner approved calibration 2ff0ffce and reports all five current Measurement videos have excellent audio delivery
voice.accent: Natural slight Indian-English; perception must be verified, not inferred from an identifier
voice.enhanced_delivery_limitation: Installed engine reproduces approved baseline, but no dedicated emotion/emphasis control has been demonstrated. A modest increase from native punctuation/context needs a short actual listening calibration; do not use rate/volume/pitch effects as a substitute.

pause_policy: Original scene/prediction starts retained. Native speech synthesis only. Caption-end corrections are at most0.25seconds and never overlap the next utterance.

events.text: How many different rectangles could you build with twenty-four equal tiles?

events.text: Today we are finding factor pairs.

events.text: We will arrange whole-number rows, record matching products, and use those pairs to find every factor without missing one.

events.text: Factors are whole numbers that multiply to make a product.
events.spoken_punctuation: Factors are whole numbers that multiply to make a product.

events.text: A factor pair gives the number of rows and the number in each row of a rectangular array.
events.spoken_punctuation: A factor pair gives the number of rows and the number in each row of a rectangular array.

events.text: Exact division tells us whether a proposed row size works.

events.text: Picture twenty-four tiles in four equal rows of six.
events.spoken_punctuation: Picture twenty-four tiles in four equal rows of six.

events.text: The row count and tiles in each row form a factor pair.

events.text: Start with twenty-four tiles.

events.text: One row of twenty-four works.

events.text: Two rows of twelve work too, as do three rows of eight and four rows of six.
events.spoken_punctuation: Two rows of twelve work too, as do three rows of eight and four rows of six!

events.text: The factors are one, two, three, four, six, eight, twelve and twenty-four.
events.spoken_punctuation: The factors are one, two, three, four, six, eight, twelve and twenty-four.

events.text: After four and six, later successful pairs repeat earlier pairs in reverse.
events.spoken_punctuation: After four and six, later successful pairs repeat earlier pairs in reverse.

events.text: For thirty-six tiles, begin with one and thirty-six, two and eighteen, three and twelve, and four and nine.

events.text: The repeated factor makes a square array, and later pairs repeat in reverse.
